findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus,
findings.note: Late subject: 12 words before the subject “I.”
The noun “decision” names the action, while the weak verb “was made” carries it.
The noun "attempt" buries the verb "attempt" behind the weak verb "is".
The verb 'cleared' is used twice within two sentences, in 'bus routes are cleared first' and 'The sidewalks along Fenwick Road are cleared by city crews'.
"picturesque" is used twice in two sentences, first in "I pass a picturesque row of Victorian houses on Linden Street".
Empty figure: "argument" casts the cold as a case or an advocate, but the draft develops no sense of any opposing voice or case, so the image does no work here.

findings.quote: People ask me why, and I have never had a good answer, so this is my attempt at one.
findings.note: Throat-clearing. The sentence announces the attempt to explain before providing the explanation.

findings.quote: It should be noted that I am not trying to tell anyone else how to live.
findings.note: Throat-clearing. The sentence frames the paragraph before its content begins.
The opening introduces the cold, an element not named in the preceding sentence, which concerned the narrator's view of the walk; the connection appears only in the predicate.

findings.quote: Municipal snow contracts in our city specify
findings.note: The sentence opens on municipal snow contracts, a new element; the previous sentence was about arriving at the desk with wet socks and a temper, and the connection to clearing appears only later in the sentence.
“The board” opens three consecutive sentences.

findings.quote: Given the results of the pilot and what both teams told us in the May retrospective,
findings.note: Late subject: 16 words before the subject, 'I'.

findings.quote: It was decided in 2023 that all changes would go through this process
findings.note: The draft never says who made this 2023 decision.

findings.quote: Concerns have been raised about the delays
findings.note: The draft does not say who raised the concerns.
The noun 'review' buries the action verb behind the weak verb 'conduct'.
The noun “determination” is buried under the weak verb “makes.”
The noun 'criticism' carries the action, while the weak verb 'is' does little work.
The doubled pair "full and complete" occurs in the third sentence.

The opening introduces admission controllers, while the previous sentence concerns leads recording approvals in release tickets. The connection appears only later, in the reference to a ticket lacking a link.
Mixed figure: the second image conflicts with the first, and the draft leaves the relationship between them unexplained.
Restatement of the result already stated as "both teams cut their median wait from six days to under one, and neither shipped a change that had to be rolled back."

findings.quote: As noted above, the board would still review every high-risk change, and nothing in this proposal would change that. Oversight would remain in place for the changes where it matters most, and that point should not be lost.
findings.note: Restatement of the earlier point, "The board would continue to meet, but only for changes that touch billing, authentication or customer data."

findings.quote: the pilot gives us limited evidence on this.
findings.note: Stacked qualification of the limitation already stated as "Two months is a short period".

findings.quote: In the weeks after the water went down and the loss adjuster had come round to photograph each and every room,
findings.note: Late subject: 21 words before the subject, Ellen.
The noun 'undertaking' buries the action of promising, carried by the weak light verb 'given'.
The action noun 'decision' is buried in the weak verb 'made'.

findings.quote: Gluten development depends on water temperature more than most home bakers realise.
findings.note: An aside: the sentence opens on gluten development, which is not connected to the preceding account of Ellen and Tom's baking arrangements, while the next sentence returns to Ellen's bread sales.
The draft never says who issued the flood warnings or why they were delayed.
The draft never says who promised the sandbags, although the failure to deliver them matters.
Stock image: the phrase supplies urgency in place of any claim about what the street had neglected and now had to do.
Stock image: the surge cliché stands in for the concrete help the street gave, which the paragraph never describes.

findings.quote: lit a fire under the council
findings.note: Stock image: this idiom substitutes for the actual pressure or response the support exerted on the council, which the paragraph leaves unspecified.
The doubled pair "each and every" occurs in the first sentence; its two parts are redundant.
“sodden” is repeated within two sentences, first in “the smell of sodden flour”.
The word “affected” is repeated within three sentences, first in “The flood affected many people on Quay Street”.

findings.quote: It is difficult to overstate how much the flood affected the people of the street
findings.note: Restatement of "The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways."
The draft never says who conducted the meeting, yet the hidden actor bears responsibility for its unproductive manner.
